chunks: And whatever is narrated from Abu Al-Rabi' Al-Shami, I have narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Muhammad bin Al-Husayn bin Abi Al-Khattab, from Al-Hakam bin Miskin, from Al-Hasan bin Ribaat, from Abu Al-Rabi' Al-Shami.

key_terms.أَبِي الرَّبِيعِ الشَّامِيِّ: Abu Al-Rabi' Al-Shami, a prominent narrator
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ بْنُ رِبَاطٍ: Al-Hasan bin Ribaat, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الْحَكَمُ بْنُ مِسْكِينٍ: Al-Hakam bin Miskin, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for the father
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd bin Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain of Abu Al-Rabi' Al-Shami verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the isnad for narrations from Abu Al-Rabi' Al-Shami by asserting he received them directly from his father, thereby validating the chain through the prominent scholar Saad ibn Abdullah. This biographical note underscores the importance of direct transmission (samāʿ) in establishing the reliability of hadith within the Shia scholarly tradition.
